note: Chapter 6 dialogue, Long Light (Willow Bend, San Lazaro, Port Linden) and the epilogue, Spring 1900. Original writing.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. Don't shoot. It's Asa. I came back. I said I wouldn't, and I came back.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You've got one minute, Asa. Use it well.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Eben's coming at dawn with Pell's warrants and Ashby's men. Twenty riders. He means to burn this place and call it the law.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Why tell me?

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Because you let me go, and he never let anybody go in his life. I'd like to be the other kind.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Riders! Twenty of them, and a sheriff's star on the one in front! That's Pell's paper with guns on it!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Everybody behind the wagons. Billy, the horses. Doc, keep your bag where you can reach it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hold the wagons! Nobody gets near the fire!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Billy, take everyone west. I'll draw them east. We meet at San Lazaro.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Ruth, Eben's with them. Up front. He's reading something.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He'll be reading Ecclesiastes. He always is, before.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell! I'll be at the old mission at San Lazaro! Come alone or bring the whole sorry choir! I've room in the churchyard!

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A man who issues invitations to his own funeral. I almost admire him. Almost.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: They burned the wagon. Hap's cook pot's still in the ashes. Somebody pick it up.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: San Lazaro. Four walls, no roof, and a bell nobody's rung in fifty years.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. You came. I knew you would. Widows are punctual; it's the waiting that teaches them.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: For everything there is a season. I read that over your husband. Did anyone tell you? I read it over all of them. It seemed only decent.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You shot him in the door of the car while he had his hands up.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: He had them half up. Messengers always think they've got time. It's a professional weakness.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Eben. Put it down. It's done. Cutter's done, I'm done. Put it down.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: Asa. Little brother. You always did hold the horses for the wrong side.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: Pell built a railroad on paper, and I built it on men like your husband. Somebody always pays for the iron. I only collected.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then here's the bill.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No more verses, Eben.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: You missed. You never miss. They told me you never miss.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I didn't. Get up, Eben. You're going to a courtroom, and you can read your verses to a jury.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: Ten past four. Was that it? I always wondered what time it was.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It was ten past four, Eben. It's been ten past four ever since.

lines.speaker: eben
lines.line: You'll be me, Caddell. By spring you'll be me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: By spring I'll be worse.

lines.speaker: ashby
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. The men need a chief now. Mr. Pell pays well, and he isn't particular.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tell Mr. Pell the price went up.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Thank you. For not doing it in front of me.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: He was my brother. I'll bury him. Somebody ought to who doesn't hate him.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: You were the other kind. You were. What happened to you?

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Front page, column one: every name in Pell's ledger and the date he paid for it. The press ran all night. My windows are broken and I've never been happier.

lines.speaker: marshal
lines.line: Mr. Pell. I've a warrant from the territorial court, sworn on your own ledger. You'll want your hat.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. I underestimated you. Not your aim. Your patience. It's the rarer gift.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I learned it from a lawyer.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. Eben is dead, I hear. A tragedy. He was my most efficient employee. I'll have to hire two to replace him.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You'll never stand in a courtroom, will you?

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: Courtrooms are where my clients stand, Mrs. Caddell. I sit behind them.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Ruth. Let's go. Please. Let's just go.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: All right, Billy. Let's go.

lines.speaker: pell
lines.line: You're robbing my office. With my own detectives. Do you hear how that sounds?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Like business, Mr. Pell. You taught the whole territory how it sounds.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: This isn't what we came for, Ruth. I don't know who you are any more. I'm not sure you do.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's over, Tom. Shale's in a cell and Pell's in the paper. I don't know what I'm supposed to do now.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Ten past four. Let's find out what time it really is.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Nobody's waiting at Willow Bend. That's all right. Nobody waits for the likes of me.

lines.speaker: fenn
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. I'm told you'll want to read about yourself. I'd advise against it. I wrote it kindly, and it still reads like an obituary.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Green on the cottonwoods. Water in the Dry Fork. Spring came anyway. It always does, they tell me.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: We're breaking camp, Ruth. Ingrid's hiring, Doc's hung a shingle in Mesquite Wells, and Del's opening a gaming house that's very nearly honest.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Horses are packed. California? Oregon? I don't care. You choose. You always choose better than me.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: They took the coffee pot. That's fair. I never made it right.

lines.speaker: ingrid
lines.line: Calves on the south section and the deeds back in my name. Come to supper. Bring whoever you've got left.

lines.speaker: ines
lines.line: Señora Ruth! Watch me run to the well and back! Doctor Abernathy says I'm a scandal!

lines.speaker: rosa
lines.line: The old well's still bitter. Mateo dug a new one. Slower, but it's ours, and nobody has a paper for it.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: The contract held till the thaw. Then Pell's lawyers came up the canyon. We're still fighting. We're good at it now.

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: Garrity's in the territorial jail and the drifts are timbered. Tommy's girl in Cardiff gets his wages. You did that, missus.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: Eben Shale's trial is set for May. I'll be testifying. Imagine that. Me, under oath, and meaning it.

lines.speaker: mabry
lines.line: Pell's building a new depot. Bigger. Some things don't change, Mrs. Caddell. I'm one of them, mostly.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Hap would've liked spring here. He'd have said the cottonwoods were showing off.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tom. It's spring. I've set the watch. It's later than I thought.
